summary: All four round-1 findings verified fixed, each by measurement in the reviewer tree rather than by reading the diff. R1a (no chain identity): AckEvent carries an epoch, the confirmed set and the watermark are keyed on it; keying the confirmed set on a constant (0L) instead of e.epoch() FAILS 1 test, so the cross-chain bleed is pinned. R1a false positive: the base is now min(sequence) per epoch; forcing it to literal 0 FAILS 1 test and forcing Math::max FAILS 3. R1b (depth-2 only): rewriting the ordering arm as !seen.contains(e.sequence()-1) -- the adjacent-only simplification -- FAILS 1 test, so anAckOverAGapOfTWOIsCaught closes it. R1c (O(N^2)): MEASURED in the reviewer tree, warm, staged bytes -- 1,000 acks 1.4ms, 5,000 8.4ms, 10,000 7.6ms, 200,000 29ms, 1,000,000 93ms, against round 1's 6ms / 110ms / 208ms / 75,353ms for the same N. Linear, and the O(highest-sequence) shape is gone: a 1,000-ack trace based at sequence 5,000,000,000 now costs 0.0004ms. R1d correctly deferred to M4.22 with a note under that row. Dropping the watermark advance loop FAILS 4 tests, turning `else if` into `if` FAILS 1, stubbing the own-write-unconfirmed arm FAILS 2. Cost lens: checkAckOrder issues no get/put/list/stat, touches no store, and the diff is test sources and backlog prose only -- the object-store request rate is unchanged. Scope: no production file moved; the row moved to backlog-done and its archive text states the by-accident and no-trace-in-production caveats rather than hiding them. Two minors, one of which is the semantic decision I was asked to judge, and I endorse it with a constraint on M4.13.

findings.title: Surviving mutation: nothing pins the WATERMARK to its epoch, so R1a's cross-chain bleed returns silently if the three maps are ever collapsed
findings.detail: The R1a fix has two halves -- the confirmed SET is per epoch, and the ordering POSITION (the watermark) is per epoch. Only the first is pinned. MEASURED in the reviewer tree against the staged bytes: replacing both `watermark.computeIfAbsent(e.epoch(), ...)` calls and `watermark.put(e.epoch(), w)` with a single shared key (0L), leaving the confirmed set correctly per-epoch, passes ALL TEN tests in AckOrderTest (BUILD SUCCESSFUL, --rerun-tasks). It is not an equivalent mutant: on the trace [confirmed(1,0), acked(1,0), confirmed(1,1), acked(1,1), confirmed(1,2), acked(1,2), confirmed(2,0), acked(2,0), confirmed(2,2), acked(2,2)] the staged checker returns `epoch 2 acked sequence 2 while the lower-numbered write 1 was still unconfirmed` and the mutant returns []. The reason the suite cannot see it is that no trace in AckOrderTest interleaves two epochs at all: ONECHAINSConfirmationsDoNotSatisfyANOTHERS runs epoch 1 to completion and then has epoch 2 ack a sequence it never confirmed, which exercises the FIRST arm (`!seen.contains(e.sequence())`) and never reaches the watermark comparison. Filed minor, not major, because the staged code is correct and this constrains a future edit, not today's behaviour.
findings.failure_scenario: M4.13 feeds the simulation's failover trace in, where epoch 1 and epoch 2 events genuinely interleave. Someone simplifying checkAckOrder -- three maps keyed on epoch is the obvious thing to collapse, and the watermark was the last of the three to be added -- hoists the watermark to a single `long`. Every test still passes. From then on, a successor chain that acks its sequence N with its own N-1 still in flight is reported CLEAN whenever the predecessor's watermark has already run past N, which is the normal case since the predecessor is the chain that was ahead. That is R1a's exact false negative, reintroduced against a green suite, in the one place M4.13 can produce it.
findings.mutation: Invariants.java:150 and 158 `watermark.computeIfAbsent(e.epoch(), base::get)` / `watermark.put(e.epoch(), w)` -> keyed on constant 0L. MEASURED: 10/10 AckOrderTest pass.
findings.fix: One test: a trace interleaving two epochs where the successor's own lower write is unconfirmed but its own sequence IS confirmed -- the ten-event trace above -- asserting exactly one violation naming `epoch 2` and `lower-numbered write 1`.

findings.title: The trace's own floor is the right base, but it makes a chain's FIRST lost write unjudgeable -- and that is a contract M4.13 has to satisfy, not a note
findings.detail: I am asked to judge basing on the trace's floor rather than a caller-supplied base, and I endorse it: a checker that invents a base it was not given is how the round-1 false positive happened, the javadoc states the consequence rather than hiding it, and a gap INSIDE the observed range is still caught -- MEASURED, [confirmed(4,1), acked(4,1), confirmed(4,3), acked(4,3)] returns `epoch 4 acked sequence 3 while the lower-numbered write 2 was still unconfirmed`. What the javadoc does not say is which case the floor rule actually costs, and it is a specific one. MEASURED: [confirmed(4,2), acked(4,2), confirmed(4,3), acked(4,3)] returns [] -- a chain whose FIRST observed write is the one that was lost is clean, because the floor moves up to the survivor. CommitLog.open writes the CONTINUE at slot 0 and CommitLog.java:192 advances nextSequence past it, so a chain's first COMMIT is at 1; if M4.13 traces only COMMITs, then a fresh leader that pipelines its first two commits, loses sequence 1 and acks sequence 2 is exactly this shape and is reported clean. The mitigation is real but partial and belongs written down: the structural residue of that run -- an empty slot 1, or an ack past a SEAL -- is caught by checkChain's `gap` and I5 arms, so a sweep running BOTH checkers is not blind, and one running only checkAckOrder is.
findings.failure_scenario: M4.13 wires the trace in and emits a confirmed event per COMMIT only. A seed drives a takeover; epoch 4 opens, pipelines its first two commits, sequence 1 loses its PUT and sequence 2 lands and is acked. checkAckOrder sees [confirmed(4,2), acked(4,2)] for that chain, takes 2 as the floor, and returns []. The seed is recorded as upholding the ack-ordering clause in the one scenario ADR-0011 names for a fresh leader. It is caught only if the sweep also runs checkChain over the same run and nobody filters its `gap` rows.
findings.fix: Either have M4.13 emit a confirmed event for the chain's slot-0 CONTINUE, which pins the floor at 0 and removes the hole entirely, or state on checkAckOrder that the caller must include the chain's first slot in the trace for the first write to be judgeable. Do NOT add a caller-supplied base parameter: the floor is derivable once slot 0 is traced, and an unchecked parameter is a second thing to get wrong.
